pytest.note: counts are from tests/test_taskspace_r10_n600_maximum_inverse_fitter.py; 0.77s is honest -- the fixture is pair_count=2 at 16x20, and n600 execution is refused without execute_reviewed + a governance callback

findings.what: Inverted clip bounds silently produce a negative-start slice and a wrong recorded statistic. _source_residual_support_labels does np.clip(row, radius + 1, height - radius - 2); when height < 2*radius + 3 the lower bound exceeds the upper bound and np.clip returns the upper bound, after which r0 = row - radius goes NEGATIVE and 'labels[pair, r0:r1, c0:c1] = 1' becomes a wrap-around slice. This is reachable with a config the dataclass ACCEPTS, because the only guard is 'support_radius_px <= min(height,width)//2' (line 191). VERIFIED by running it: height=width=16, support_radius_px=8 is accepted; clip lower=9 > upper=6; center clipped to (6,6); r0=-2; only 1 pixel is actually labelled while the emitted row records support_pixels=289 -- a 289x wrong sufficient statistic, with no error raised. The polygon that _polygon_from_support (line 843) then derives clamps with max(0,...) and describes a 17x17 box that does not match the 1-pixel mask, so the counted PULLBACK_POLYGON operand and the encoder-side support disagree. Default/realistic geometry (874x1164, radius 8) is safe -- this bites small-geometry smokes, which is precisely where wrong numbers are least likely to be noticed.
findings.fix: Two changes, both needed: (1) tighten the config guard at line 191 to 'support_radius_px <= (min(height,width) - 3) // 2' so the clip range can never invert; (2) record the MEASURED count, int(np.count_nonzero(labels[pair_index])), instead of the intended box area (r1-r0)*(c1-c0) at line 769, so the receipt reports what happened rather than what was intended.

findings.what: Buffer aliasing trap. All three _source_residual_support_labels calls (lines 1453, 1934, 2065) pass the same 'label_output' buffer, so support_labels from line 1934 and _polygon_labels from line 2065 are the SAME ndarray object. findings.what: _fit_texture_record hardcodes texture_gain_q8=256 in every candidate (lines 818 and 830) and never fits it, so the counted TEXTURE gain operand is a constant 2 bytes per pair -- 1,200 bytes at n600 -- carrying zero fitted information. solver_by_section honestly says 'finite frequency-phase plus analytic amplitude inverse' (line 2380), so this is not a false claim, but it is pure rate cost in a module whose purpose is minimizing counted bytes.
findings.fix: Either fit texture_gain_q8 (it is already a reachable operand -- mutate_r10_constraint('TEXTURE') moves it), or hoist it to a single packet-level constant instead of one per pair.

findings.what: The full-resolution XIP2 acceptance control loops 'for _control_pass in range(config.pair_count + 1)' and each pass performs 2 full-resolution warps for every pair. Worst case is O(P^2) full-resolution warps -- up to ~720,000 at P=600. Termination is correct (each pass zeroes at least one previously-nonzero row and a zeroed row can never re-enter 'worsening'), so the loop is sound; the concern is only the worst-case cost at the module's own n600 target.
findings.fix: Cap the pass count with an explicit budget and record the cap in the trace, or zero all worsening rows for the pass in one shot and re-check once.

no_fake_notes: n600 naming is NOT a prefix fake. pair_count is an explicit config field validated to [1,600] (line 163); pair_count==600 is refused unless execute_reviewed=True (line 201) AND a live governance callback returns required/verified (lines 1221-1230, re-checked before every stage and range publish at lines 1262 and 1272). Every scientific-authority field is structurally forced to None -- R10SectionFitV1.__post_init__ (lines 236-240) RAISES if d_seg, d_pose, complete_candidate_zip_bytes or score_units_per_byte is populated -- and full_n600_receiver_measured_exhaustion is False (line 2450). The tests run at pair_count=2, which is legal SCOPE reduction with honest labels, not a measurement claim on a prefix.

'fitter' is NOT a search mislabelled as a solver (NO-FAKE class 6). _fit_base_feature_record performs a genuine np.linalg.lstsq normal-equation solve plus an SVD rank-one projection (lines 684-685) before coordinate refinement, and _fit_pitch_and_xi is coordinate descent with a full-resolution acceptance control. The parts that ARE enumerative (pitch lattice, texture frequency/phase grid, flow translation grid) are labelled 'finite ... lattice' in solver_by_section (lines 2376-2386) and their candidate lists are emitted in the trace, so the search is disclosed rather than dressed up.
